analysis:
Examined both SetupCommand head excerpts and SetupProgress metadata, patch and BASE source against the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. New behavior accepts repeated work disks, checks them before installation, offers external disks interactively, and optionally enables ownership after explicit confirmation (SandboxSetupCommand.swift:297-367). Root execution remains refused at 84-88. Disk requests require installer feature support (482-486); a failed disk-aware plan aborts rather than using an internal-disk estimate (435-446). SetupProgress.swift's added disk parser (head patch:195-204) and bounded numeric choice loop (486-499) introduce no independently demonstrated security regression.
Relevant boundaries are TB-013/T-061/A-019 (owner-account installer execution), TB-012/T-059/A-018 (VM/provider availability), and TB-003/T-016 (disk exhaustion). The shown code does not change provider authorization, attestation, traffic encryption, key custody, billing enforcement or prefix-cache storage. T-041's encrypted external-cache requirements cannot be assumed to protect sandbox work disks; these are distinct data paths. Existing shell execution and untrusted installer rendering are not new findings.
Integration must examine SandboxWorkDisk.absolutePath/volume/check/candidates/enableOwnership, SandboxInstaller.supportsDisks/arguments/planArguments, and the add-on work-disk implementation. Verify privileged diskutil invocation uses fixed executables and separate arguments, selected volumes are revalidated against mount replacement, disk paths survive option serialization safely, and refusal while jobs run preserves payment and provider hold behavior (SetupCommand.swift:535-538 states an external installer contract, not verified enforcement). Determine whether TB-013/A-019 and availability documentation need explicit removable-work-disk coverage. Missing implementations and selected-only threat definitions limit conclusions; no missing external control is asserted as a vulnerability.
